body.title: Refresh AGENTS.md and keep it in sync with the codebase
body.description:
## Summary

`AGENTS.md` is the main guide agents read before working in this repository, but nothing keeps it accurate. It drifts as commands, flags, helpers, and `make` targets change, and agents follow it word for word.

Example: it tells agents to pass **only** the discussion ID to `glab mr note resolve`. That fails as soon as `--repo` is set, because the merge request is then required and comes first (see https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4192 and https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8404).

## Proposal

### 1. Refresh `AGENTS.md`

Check every instruction against the current tree and fix or remove what is out of date:

- `glab` invocations: commands, argument order, flags.
- Helper and example paths (`internal/cmdutils/`, `internal/testing/cmdtest/`, the canonical example files).
- `make` targets, `lefthook` jobs, scripts, environment variables.

### 2. Keep it up to date continuously

Options, which can be combined:

- **CI check**: parse `AGENTS.md` and fail when it references something that no longer exists:
  - every `glab <noun> <verb>` resolves in the cobra command tree, and every `--flag` is defined on it;
  - every repository path exists;
  - every `make` target and `lefthook` job exists.
- **Review rule**: add a block to `.gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml` that asks Duo Code Review to flag MRs that rename or remove something `AGENTS.md` mentions without updating it.
- **Scheduled refresh**: a scheduled pipeline or agent flow that compares `AGENTS.md` with the tree and opens an MR when they differ.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` is accurate against `main`.
- [ ] At least one automated mechanism catches drift before or soon after merge.

---
_Drafted with an AI agent (Claude Code)._

body.title: glab release create and upload panic on a null entry in --assets-links
body.description:
### Summary

When the JSON array given to `--assets-links` contains `null`, `glab release create` and `glab release upload` crash with `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` and exit status 2. Both commands decode the flag into `[]*upload.ReleaseAsset` ([create.go#L244-249](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/a6fd50cecb4bbe630dfb03a621cbe2cedfef4aef/internal/commands/release/create/create.go#L244-249), [upload.go#L138-143](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/a6fd50cecb4bbe630dfb03a621cbe2cedfef4aef/internal/commands/release/upload/upload.go#L138-143)), so a `null` element becomes a nil pointer, and the commands dereference every link later on, first in `aliasFilePathToDirectAssetPath` ([releaseutils/upload/upload.go#L270-271](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/a6fd50cecb4bbe630dfb03a621cbe2cedfef4aef/internal/commands/release/releaseutils/upload/upload.go#L270-271)).

By the time glab crashes, it may already have changed the release:

- `glab release upload` adds the links that come before the `null` one.
- `glab release create` on an existing release updates the release and adds the links that come before the `null` one.
- `glab release create` for a new release creates it and adds the links that come before the `null` one in v1.124.0. On `main`, which sends the links in the create request since !4040, it crashes before the release is created.

So a `null` in the array can leave the release partly updated, and what the user sees is a Go stack trace rather than an error about the flag.

### Environment

- OS: Linux x86_64 (a `golang:1.27.3` container)
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: none (the commands ran without a terminal)
- GLAB: v1.124.0, built from the tag, and `main` at a6fd50cecb4bbe630dfb03a621cbe2cedfef4aef

Other: I did not run this against a GitLab instance. glab talked to a small local HTTP server that answers the tag and release endpoints the way GitLab does and logs every request it receives, which is where the request lists below come from.

### Steps to reproduce

In a project where you can create releases and that has the tag `v1.0.0` (from a clone of it, or with `-R <group>/<project>`):

```shell
# A release that does not exist yet
glab release create v1.0.0 --notes x --assets-links='[{"name":"a","url":"https://example.com/a"}, null]'

# A release that exists. On main the command above does not create it,
# so create it first with: glab release create v1.0.0 --notes x
glab release create v1.0.0 --notes x --assets-links='[{"name":"b","url":"https://example.com/b"}, null]'
glab release upload v1.0.0 --assets-links='[{"name":"c","url":"https://example.com/c"}, null]'
```

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

Each command panics and exits with status 2. The first one with v1.124.0, with the progress symbols removed and the stack trace shortened:

```plaintext
Validating tag v1.0.0
Creating or updating release repo=group/proj tag=v1.0.0
Release created:	url=http://127.0.0.1:18081/group/proj/-/releases/v1.0.0
Uploading release assets repo=group/proj tag=v1.0.0
Added release asset	name=a url=https://example.com/a
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x10 pc=0x15de74f]

goroutine 1 [running]:
gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/release/releaseutils/upload.aliasFilePathToDirectAssetPath(...)
	internal/commands/release/releaseutils/upload/upload.go:220
gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/release/releaseutils/upload.CreateLink(...)
	internal/commands/release/releaseutils/upload/upload.go:54 +0x4f
gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/release/releaseutils/upload.(*Context).CreateReleaseAssetLinks(...)
	internal/commands/release/releaseutils/upload/upload.go:196 +0x152
gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/release/releaseutils.CreateReleaseAssets(...)
	internal/commands/release/releaseutils/releaseutils.go:132 +0x450
gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/release/create.createRun(...)
	internal/commands/release/create/create.go:563 +0x1d48
[...]
```

The requests each command sent before the panic:

| Command | v1.124.0 | `main` at a6fd50ce |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `release create`, new release | GET tag, GET release, POST release, POST link `a` | GET tag, GET release |
| `release create`, existing release | GET tag, GET release, PUT release, POST link `b` | GET tag, GET release, PUT release, POST link `b` |
| `release upload` | GET release, POST link `c` | GET release, POST link `c` |

On `main` the first command panics in `upload.AliasFilePaths` ([create.go#L528](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/a6fd50cecb4bbe630dfb03a621cbe2cedfef4aef/internal/commands/release/create/create.go#L528)) and the other two in `upload.CreateLink`, all at the same line of `aliasFilePathToDirectAssetPath`.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

The command refuses the flag before it sends any request, the way it already refuses malformed JSON (`failed to parse JSON string: ...`), and names the element that is `null`.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

The output and request lists above.

### Possible fixes

Decode `--assets-links` in one helper that both commands call, next to `releaseutils.AssetsFromArgs`, and return an error there for a `null` element, with its index. Both commands parse the flag before their first request (`complete` in create, `validate` in upload), so the command then fails before it changes anything. I have a merge request ready with this change and a test in each command.

body.title: Share the context-aware wait and its test hook through cmdutils
body.description:
## Summary

Two commands have the same context-aware wait with a test hook:

- `internal/commands/govern/audit/sync/sync.go`: `options.waitFor` and `options.wait`
- `internal/commands/project/fork/fork.go`: the same pair, added in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4187 for the fork import poll

Each command keeps the hook on its own `options` struct. Tests have to build `options` and call `run` directly, so the fork poll tests can't use `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest` like the other tests in `fork_test.go`.

## Proposal

Move the wait into `cmdutils` and expose it through the `Factory`, with a `cmdtest` `FactoryOption` that records the requested waits and returns at once. Then:

- Switch `govern audit sync` and `repo fork` to the shared wait.
- Move the fork import poll tests onto `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest`.

Other polling loops that sleep without checking the context, such as the 3 s ticker in `ci status`, could adopt it later.

Raised in review: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4187#note_4078613689
